text:
Sam V.: Hey all start date 7/12. Offer includes a $2k relocation reimbursement (receipts) and a monthly commuter stipend. Quick Qs: 1) Is relocation reimbursed on the payroll or as an expense reimbursement after receipts? 2) I have a civil union (domestic partner) what proof do you need? 3) My first week has a holiday will the virtual commuter card activate if I finish onboarding that week?

Aisha (People Ops): Welcome Sam! Answers: 1) If receipts required it's processed as an expense reimbursement separate from payroll. It posts to the reimbursements ledger after manager/finance approval. 2) For civil unions we accept the DP affidavit + either a civil union certificate or joint document (bank stmt, lease) dated within 60 days. 3) Virtual commuter cards usually activate after HR marks you active and direct deposit clears; holidays can delay activation by 1 business day.

Sam V.: Got it. For the reimbursement, is there a receipt template or preferred format? I have multiple receipts from movers and storage.

Marcus (Payroll): Hi Sam we have a relocation receipts template PDF in the onboarding portal under "Expense Forms." Combine receipts into a single PDF, include dates and vendor names, and attach a short explanation noting which costs are reimbursable per your offer. Once finance approves we push it to the next payable reimbursement run. Expect 2-3 weeks from approval to payment depending on cycle.

Sam V.: Thanks. Also curious about tax treatment are reimbursements taxable? What about the commuter stipend?

Marcus (Payroll): Expense reimbursements for documented business moving costs are generally non-taxable if they meet IRS substantiation rules; relocation reimbursements vary by jurisdiction. Commuter stipend can be pre-tax up to federal limits if registered as a qualified transportation benefit; otherwise it's taxable. State rules differ (e.g., CA has special rules). DM me your state and I'll run a quick net estimate for both items.

Renee (Benefits): For the civil union add-on, enroll your partner within 30 days of your start date in the benefits portal. We need DP affidavit + one supporting doc: civil union certificate, joint lease, or joint bank statement (within 60 days). If you don't have documents dated within 60 days, upload what you have and we'll advise next steps. Note: if your partner is on other primary coverage we'll need COB forms.

Sam V.: I have a civil union certificate and a shared bank statement. Uploaded both to the portal just now, status shows "pending verification."

Aisha (People Ops): Thanks Sam I see the upload. Renee, can Benefits expedite verification?

Renee (Benefits): I see it and will fast-track. Expect status change in <24h. Also FYI: adding a partner doesn't change your benefits effective date; coverage takes effect per standard new-hire elections.

Sam V.: One more I selected virtual commuter card. If I complete I-9 + direct deposit by EOD Thu, is same-day activation realistic before the holiday Fri?

Marcus (Payroll): If docs clear by EOD Thu and HR flips active status, virtual card activation before Friday is possible but not guaranteed due to holiday processing. Plan for possible 1-business-day delay. If you need transit funds immediately, we can issue a one-time manual reimbursement for transit expenses; DM me with dates/amounts and receipts.

hr-bot: Reminder: Benefits enrollment window = 30 days from start. Required docs for DP: signed DP affidavit + supporting document. New hire docs due within 3 business days.

Sam V.: Awesome, thanks everyone. I'll DM Marcus my state and upload the combined receipts PDF tonight. Appreciate the help! :thumbsup:
